clippings.speaker: Christopher Guest
clippings.quote: Eugene and I were talking about this idea of him having two left feet. And you’d think, on the face of it, Well, that’s just insane . But to play it completely real is a way of dealing with that in a different way. And I thought it worked. I guess that’s sort of self-serving, but I think it worked—because of Eugene, who was just extraordinary in that part.
clippings.title: The Oral History of 'Best in Show'
clippings.context: Guest on Levy's character Gerry Fleck, in a 20th-anniversary oral history of the film.

clippings.speaker: Eugene Levy
clippings.quote: We had done Guffman , and then [Guest] came back with this other idea about a dog show. It was a funny idea, but I said, “What do we do for a third act?” … So we kind of set it aside and started working on something else. Then about a year after that, it was “What about the dog show idea?”
clippings.title: The Oral History of 'Best in Show'
clippings.context: Levy, the film's cowriter, recalls how Guest pitched the dog-show idea and how long it sat before they cracked it.

clippings.speaker: Christopher Guest
clippings.quote: I remember during “Waiting for Guffman” near the end of the movie where Eugene was playing a comic in Florida, and I was watching the movie, and of course I didn’t know what he was going to do, and I was laughing so hard that I couldn’t look at the monitor. I was literally doubled over.
clippings.title: Interview: How to Write Your Own Script
clippings.context: Roundtable with Boston reporters promoting For Your Consideration; asked whether he finds his own films funny.

clippings.speaker: Eugene Levy
clippings.quote: You just don’t have this kind of creative flexibility and freedom. And this is the only experience that I’ve had where the creative input is exactly what you see when the movie comes out. The studio doesn’t creatively interfere. Chris [Guest] has final cut on the movie.
clippings.title: Interview: How to Write Your Own Script
clippings.context: Same Boston roundtable; Levy on why the Guest films are unlike his other movie work.

clippings.speaker: Christopher Guest
clippings.quote: The hopefully simple answer is I come up with an idea and I get together with Eugene, and we talk about whether that could be something viable in terms of its interest for both of us, and whether it can be funny and interesting, and then we set about to writing what will be a 25-page outline.
clippings.title: Christopher Guest and Eugene Levy, For Your Consideration
clippings.context: Joint interview; asked how the two work as a writing team.

notes: Levy-on-Guest is thinner and mostly about process; 1997 Philadelphia City Paper joint profile (mycitypaper.com) is dead (account suspended).
